content.comment_body: Hi everyone, I have this device [article_no], so which hardware should I select in the software [version_no] or [version_no]? I set up a configuration with some AND gates and relays using timers to keep outputs active while pulses come to the inputs, suited to our logic needs. I did the configuration in [product_name] [version_no] using hardware [product_name] [version_no], since the device wasn’t available yet, ordered it later, and sent the config file to our installer via email. When our installer received the device and went onsite for installation, I told him to select the correct hardware version in the software before uploading it to device [article_no]. Our installer got the software DVD together with the device, which was version [version_no]. First issue was selecting the correct hardware within the software, and the second was connecting to the device. How can you confirm connection is online and uploading was successful? Support advised me to upgrade the software to [version_no] to enable communication with [article_no]. It seems odd that version [version_no] wouldn’t support [article_no]. Thanks for your help. I've been working with [product_name] for about ten years, though only occasionally, with about ten devices total. So, I tend to relearn everything with each new project. We use [product_name] when our security device’s own logic isn’t sufficient.

The device with order number [article_no] is the current [product_name] [version_no]. For communication such as program transfer and online tests, you need [product_name] [version_no] or [version_no].

It's best to use the latest [version_no]. With this, you can also install the latest version of [product_name]. You can freely download the upgrade from [version_no] to [version_no], which is the service pack 1 for [product_name] [version_no]. Check this topic: Download links for current [product_name] software and firmware

Thanks [user_name]. So, should I select [article_no] Standard as the hardware in the software? The options are confusing compared to the version printed on the device. [company_name] can handle complex logic, but naming versions to match would be helpful :) I’ll upgrade to [version_no]. I saw info about [product_name] on YouTube. Looks good, but I haven't had time for that.
No, not [article_no] Standard. You need to select [product_name] [version_no] as hardware, but this requires [product_name] [version_no]. Older versions do not recognize [product_name] [version_no].
That makes sense now! Thanks a lot, [user_name]!

analysis.insight_summary: Users find it challenging to match hardware codes between the configuration software and their [product_name] device, as the identifiers in the software appear unclear. There is also confusion about software compatibility, with users learning that [product_name] [version_no] (not just [version_no]) is needed to properly connect and configure the latest [product_name] hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want hardware versions in the software to be easy to identify and directly correspond to the labeling found on their devices, as well as seamless compatibility with their hardware without needing additional software updates.
